chunks: Abu Ayyub narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:

If a man performs i‘tikaf for one day and has not made a stipulation, then he may leave and break his i‘tikaf. But if he remains for two days and has not made a stipulation, then he may not break his i‘tikaf until three days pass.

key_terms.اشْتَرَطَ: made a stipulation or condition at the outset
key_terms.اعْتَكَفَ: entered into i‘tikaf, the act of spiritual retreat in the mosque
key_terms.اعْتِكَافَهُ: his i‘tikaf, meaning his devotional retreat
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ: three days, the minimum completion period indicated here
key_terms.يَفْسَخَ: to break, dissolve, or terminate the i‘tikaf

ai.seo_question: When does i‘tikaf become binding if no stipulation was made at the beginning?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning i‘tikaf and the effect of not making a stipulation at its outset. It states that after one day a person may still leave, but after completing two days, he must continue until the completion of three days.
